   - Reverted the removal of DMA mapping support for 32-bit systems with 64-bit DMA. The check that previously returned `-EOPNOTSUPP` if `sizeof(dma_addr_t) > sizeof(unsigned long)` was removed.

2. **`include/linux/mm_types.h`**:
   - Modified the `struct page` to include a union that allows for either a `dma_addr_upper` (for 64-bit DMA addresses) or an `atomic_long_t pp_frag_count` (for fragment page support). This change accommodates the need for 64-bit addressing on 32-bit architectures.

3. **`include/net/page_pool.h`**:
   - Introduced a macro `PAGE_POOL_DMA_USE_PP_FRAG_COUNT` to determine if 64-bit DMA addressing is required on 32-bit architectures.
   - Updated the `page_pool_get_dma_addr` function to return a combined DMA address using `dma_addr_upper` if necessary.
   - Updated the `page_pool_set_dma_addr` function to set the upper bits of the DMA address when applicable.

#### Relationships Between Modifications:

The modifications across the three files are interconnected as follows:

- The changes in `net/core/page_pool.c` are directly related to the adjustments made in `include/linux/mm_types.h` and `include/net/page_pool.h`. The reintroduction of DMA mapping support necessitated the need for the union in the `struct page` to handle both 32-bit and 64-bit addressing.
- The new macro and logic in `include/net/page_pool.h` provide the necessary conditions to manage DMA addresses correctly, ensuring that the system can handle both types of architectures without breaking functionality.
- Overall, the patch aims to restore functionality that was lost due to the previous removal of DMA mapping support, ensuring compatibility with 32-bit systems that utilize 64-bit DMA addressing.

   - Modified the `struct page` to include a union that allows for either a `dma_addr_upper` or an `atomic_long_t pp_frag_count`, enabling support for 64-bit DMA addresses on 32-bit architectures.

#### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the three files are interconnected as follows:

- The changes in `include/net/page_pool.h` and `include/linux/mm_types.h` establish a new mechanism for handling DMA addresses that can accommodate 64-bit values on 32-bit architectures. This is crucial for the functionality of the page pool when DMA mapping is enabled.

The new checks ensure that the system can still handle cases where fragment counts are involved, thus maintaining stability while re-enabling DMA mapping support.

content: You are a programming expert.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug was caused by enabling LPAE (Large Physical Address Extension) on 32-bit systems, which automatically enabled `CONFIG_ARCH_DMA_ADDR_T_64BIT`. This change led to a situation where the DMA mapping support was not compatible with the page pool's handling of DMA addresses, specifically when the `PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP` flag was used by Ethernet drivers. The previous removal of DMA mapping support did not account for active consumers, resulting in a broken boot process when these drivers attempted to use the page pool.
        
        Commit message:
        page_pool: Revert "page_pool: disable dma mapping support..."

This reverts commit d00e60ee54b12de945b8493cf18c1ada9e422514.

As reported by Guillaume in [1]:
Enabling LPAE always enables CONFIG_ARCH_DMA_ADDR_T_64BIT
in 32-bit systems, which breaks the bootup proceess when a
ethernet driver is using page pool with PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP flag.
As we were hoping we had no active consumers for such system
when we removed the dma mapping support, and LPAE seems like
a common feature for 32 bits system, so revert it.

1. https://www.spinics.net/lists/netdev/msg779890.html

Fixes: d00e60ee54b1 ("page_pool: disable dma mapping support for 32-bit arch with 64-bit DMA")
Signed-off-by: Yunsheng Lin <linyunsheng@huawei.com>
Reported-by: "kernelci.org bot" <bot@kernelci.org>
Tested-by: "kernelci.org bot" <bot@kernelci.org>
Acked-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Acked-by: Ilias Apalodimas <ilias.apalodimas@linaro.org>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/net/core/page_pool.c b/net/core/page_pool.c
index 9b60e4301a44..1a6978427d6c 100644
--- a/net/core/page_pool.c
+++ b/net/core/page_pool.c
@@ -49,12 +49,6 @@ static int page_pool_init(struct page_pool *pool,
 	 * which is the XDP_TX use-case.
 	 */
 	if (pool->p.flags & PP_FLAG_DMA_MAP) {
-		/* DMA-mapping is not supported on 32-bit systems with
-		 * 64-bit DMA mapping.
-		 */
-		if (sizeof(dma_addr_t) > sizeof(unsigned long))
-			return -EOPNOTSUPP;
-
 		if ((pool->p.dma_dir != DMA_FROM_DEVICE) &&
 		    (pool->p.dma_dir != DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL))
 			return -EINVAL;
@@ -75,6 +69,10 @@ static int page_pool_init(struct page_pool *pool,
 		 */
 	}
 
+	if (PAGE_POOL_DMA_USE_PP_FRAG_COUNT &&
+	    pool->p.flags & PP_FLAG_PAGE_FRAG)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	if (ptr_ring_init(&pool->ring, ring_qsize, GFP_KERNEL) < 0)
 		return -ENOMEM;
